implementation_summary: AC-EDIT-7 was ALREADY correctly satisfied by prior work before this story began: S2's mechanical field-swap made `applyDeleteEditSignal` derive `senderPubkey = sender?.pubkey ?? rumor.pubkey` and compare it (DELETE via `authorizeDeleteAgainstTarget(threadKey, knownRow.content, senderPubkey, knownRow.senderPubkey)`; EDIT via `pubkeysMatch(senderPubkey, knownRow.senderPubkey)`) against `knownRow.senderPubkey`, which chatHandler.ts:86 (also S2) populates from the authenticated sender. The admin-delete carve-out already existed independently (epic-group-invite-lifecycle's DD-11/AC-IMMUT-4/5, `GroupAdminsProvider`), scoped to GROUP-thread informative-announcement targets only, and already keys its admin lookup on the same authenticated `senderPubkey` value (never `rumor.pubkey`) — confirmed by reading `authorizeDeleteAgainstTarget`/`groupAdminsFor`/`isAdminPubkey` in messageEdits/api.ts. The third-hop inheritance (chatPersistence.ts's `TombstoneAuthorization`) was also already correct: `TombstoneAuthorization.senderPubkeyHex` is populated exclusively from the caller-supplied `incoming.senderPubkeyHex` in `applyToKnownSlotCore`; `tombstoneMessage` never reads `rumor.pubkey` or any other forgeable field independently. No production code was changed in messageEdits/api.ts, deleteEditHandler.ts, or chatPersistence.ts. deleteEditHandler.ts:29-56's trust-model comment block was read and left byte-for-byte untouched. This story's entire diff is test-coverage: added an 'AC-EDIT-7 (S4)' describe block (8 new tests) to app/tests/unit/marmot/groupMessageEdits.test.ts, calling `applyDeleteEditSignal` directly (handler-unit level, real idb-keyval-backed storage, no spies on the authorization decision itself): (a) own-author delete/edit accepted (2 tests); (b) cross-author delete/edit rejected — ordinary-message delete, announcement delete by a non-admin (fail-closed empty admin set), and edit rejected even when the signer IS a registered admin (AC-IMMUT-6: edit never gets an admin carve-out) (3 tests); (c) the admin-delete path tested as its own distinct case, with rumor.pubkey and the authenticated `sender` deliberately swapped across the two tests so a naive rumor.pubkey fallback anywhere in the admin-check chain (including chatPersistence.ts) would flip at least one outcome — this doubles as direct evidence for the third-hop inheritance claim against real (non-mocked) storage (2 tests); (d) one combined fail-closed check asserting the target row is byte-for-byte unchanged (`toEqual`) after a rejected delete and a rejected edit.
